ps8.title: Night Sky
ps8.setting: What is man? — the night sky of creation
ps8.intro: A night in the fields with not a single lamp, and the sky was full of stars. David looked up at that sky and asked why the One who made the moon and stars with his fingers would remember a small human being. It is a song with a heading that says to sing it to the Gittith.

lines.주의 이름 온 땅에: Your name in all the earth
lines.주의 영광 하늘에 두셨네: You set your glory above the heavens
lines.어린 아이와 젖먹이의 입으로: From the mouths of children and infants
lines.주께서 펼쳐 놓으신 달과 별들: The moon and stars you set in place
lines.제가 그 하늘을 올려다볼 때: When I lift my eyes to that sky
lines.사람이 무엇이기에 주께서 기억하시며: What is man that you remember him
lines.인생이 무엇이기에 보살피시나요: What are we, that you care for us

lines.영광과 존귀로 왕관 씌우셨네: and crowned us with glory and honor
lines.모든 양과 소떼: All the sheep and the herds

lines.온 땅에 가득한 주의 아름다운 이름: Your beautiful name fills all the earth

ps19.title: The Heavens Speak
ps19.setting: The sky and the Word — two books
ps19.intro: The sun rose at the eastern edge and ran from one end of the sky to the other. David sang that the silent heavens declare God's handiwork day after day, and then he sang of the Lord's law that revives the soul. It is a song of two books: the sky and the Word.

lines.하늘이 하나님의 영광을 말하고: The heavens tell the glory of God
lines.궁창이 그 손으로 하신 일을 알리네: The sky proclaims the work of his hands

ps104.title: The World He Made
ps104.setting: Sea and mountains, beasts and people — a song of creation
ps104.intro: No author's name remains on this song. The singer recalled the beginning, when God, wearing light like a garment, laid the foundations of the earth and set a boundary for the sea. Then he praised him, calling out one by one the wild donkeys of the hills, the birds in their nests, and even the ships on the sea.

lines.내 영혼아 여호와를 송축하라: Bless the Lord, O my soul

ps90.title: A Prayer in the Wilderness
ps90.setting: Moses' prayer at the end of forty years in the wilderness (heading)
ps90.intro: This song carries the heading, a prayer of Moses, the man of God. For forty years in the wilderness Moses watched a whole generation fall on the sand. He set our short lives before the everlasting God and asked for wisdom to number our days.

lines.주여 주는 대대로: Lord, you have been our dwelling place
lines.산이 생기기 전 땅이 지어지기 전: Before the mountains, before the earth

ps114.title: The Sea Looked and Fled
ps114.setting: The day the Red Sea and the Jordan parted
ps114.intro: The day Israel came out of Egypt, the sea made a way, and forty years later the Jordan stopped flowing. A singer whose name is lost bound those two days into one song and asked the sea and the mountains why they were so startled.

lines.이스라엘이 애굽에서 나올 때: When Israel came out of Egypt
lines.야곱의 집이 낯선 말의 백성을 떠날 때: when Jacob's house left a foreign people
lines.바다야 너는 어찌하여 도망하느냐: O sea, why is it that you flee?

ps105.title: The God Who Remembers His Covenant
ps105.setting: From Abraham to the Exodus — remember
ps105.intro: Chronicles tells that on the day David brought the ark up to Jerusalem, Asaph and his brothers gave thanks with the first part of this song. The song begins with the covenant made with Abraham, passes through Joseph and Moses, and goes on to the manna in the wilderness and the water from the rock, singing in order the things God remembered.

lines.여호와께 감사하며 그 이름을 부르라: Give thanks to the Lord, call on his name
lines.그가 하신 일을 만민에게 알리라: Make known his deeds among the peoples

ps68.title: God Arises
ps68.setting: God marching from Sinai to Zion
ps68.intro: Every time the ark set out, Moses cried, Arise, O Lord! This song of David begins with that cry and sings of God marching from Mount Sinai through the wilderness to the sanctuary in Zion. Singers and young women playing tambourines followed the procession.

ps29.title: The Voice over the Waters
ps29.setting: The voice of the Lord from Lebanon to the wilderness of Kadesh
ps29.intro: A storm rolled in from the sea, broke the cedars of Lebanon, and swept south as far as the wilderness of Kadesh. In that thunder David heard the voice of the Lord. Calling on that voice seven times, he sang for the heavenly beings to give glory to God.

ps23.title: My Shepherd
ps23.setting: David the shepherd boy in the fields of Bethlehem
ps23.intro: In the fields of Bethlehem, the boy David, keeping the flock, led his sheep each day to green pastures and still waters. There were nights when wild beasts attacked. Years later he sang of what he had learned in those fields.

ps59.title: Soldiers under the Window
ps59.setting: The night Saul's soldiers watched David's house (1 Sam 19:11)
ps59.intro: The soldiers Saul sent surrounded David's house all night, planning to kill him when morning came. His wife Michal let him down through a window. It is the song sung on the night his enemies were watching the house.

ps52.title: Blood at Nob
ps52.setting: Doeg informs on them and the priests of Nob are killed (1 Sam 22)
ps52.intro: David stopped at Nob and received bread and Goliath's sword from the priest Ahimelech. Doeg the Edomite, who was there, reported it to Saul, and eighty-five priests of Nob were put to death. This is David's song when he heard the news.

ps56.title: Seized in Gath
ps56.intro: Fleeing from Saul, David went into Gath in the land of the Philistines. But the servants of King Achish recognized him as the man who killed Goliath. On the day he was seized in his enemies' city, he prayed this in his fear.

ps34.title: The Day He Feigned Madness
ps34.setting: Feigning madness before Achish and driven away (1 Sam 21:13)
ps34.intro: When his life was in danger before Achish, king of Gath, David pretended to be mad, scratching on the doors of the gate and letting spit run down his beard. The king drove him away. Walking out of the city gate alive, David sang a song of thanks.

ps142.intro: Barely escaping from Gath, David hid in the cave of Adullam. His brothers and his father's whole household came down to him there, and people in distress, in debt, and bitter in soul gathered around him. The heading says it is a prayer David offered when he was in the cave.

ps54.title: Betrayed in the Wilderness of Ziph
ps54.setting: The Ziphites tell Saul where David is hiding (1 Sam 23:19)
ps54.intro: While David was hiding in the thickets of the wilderness of Ziph, the Ziphites went up to Gibeah and told Saul where he was hiding. His own fellow men of Judah handed him over. It is the song of the day Saul's army came closing in around the hill.

ps57.setting: Sparing Saul in the cave (1 Sam 24)
ps57.intro: Near the Rocks of the Wild Goats at En-gedi, David and his men were hiding deep inside a cave. Saul came into that cave alone, but David only quietly cut off a corner of his robe and did not harm the king. The heading says it is David's song from when he was in the cave, fleeing from Saul.

ps63.intro: The wilderness of Judah is a dry, harsh land that drops steeply toward the Dead Sea. The heading says David wrote this song while he was in this wilderness. In a land without a sip of water, he thirsted for the God he had once seen in the sanctuary.

ps18.title: My Rock

ps18.intro: While David was staying at Ziklag, news reached him that Saul had died on Mount Gilboa. The long years of being hunted were over. ps24.title: The King of Glory
ps24.setting: The ark comes up to the City of David (2 Sam 6)
ps24.intro: The ark of the Lord, which had stayed three months in the house of Obed-edom, at last came up to the City of David. David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might, and all Israel shouted for joy and blew the trumpets. This song of questions and answers at the city gates was likely sung in such a procession.

ps132.title: A Vow for the Ark
ps132.setting: Until David found a place for the ark
ps132.intro: For a long time the ark stayed in the house of Abinadab in the woods of Kiriath-jearim. David swore to the Lord that he would not lie down in comfort until he had found a place for the ark. In later years, pilgrims going up to the temple remembered David's vow with this song.

ps3.intro: News reached Jerusalem that his son Absalom had been made king in Hebron. David covered his head and climbed the road up the Mount of Olives barefoot and weeping. This is the song the hunted king sang that night.

lines.땅을 적시는 단비같이 오리니: like showers that water the earth
lines.그의 날에 의인이 꽃 피고: In his days the righteous will flourish
lines.달이 다하도록 평강이 넘치리: Peace will abound till the moon is no more
lines.바다에서 바다까지: He will rule from sea to sea
lines.강에서 땅 끝까지 다스리리: from the River to the ends of the earth
lines.궁핍한 이가 부르짖을 때 건지고: He rescues the needy when they cry
lines.도울 이 없는 가난한 이를 살리리: and saves the poor who have no helper
lines.그들의 피가 그 눈에 귀하리라: Their blood is precious in his sight
lines.그의 이름이 해처럼 오래가고: May his name endure like the sun
lines.사람들이 그로 인해 복을 받으리: May people be blessed through him
lines.홀로 기이한 일을 하시는: Praise the Lord God, the God of Israel
lines.온 땅에 그의 영광이 가득하리: May his glory fill the whole earth

ps127.title: The One Who Builds the House
ps127.intro: Solomon spent seven years building the temple of the Lord and thirteen years building his own palace. This song, bearing the name of the king who built the temple and the palace, asks who it is that builds the house. In later years, pilgrims going up to the temple also sang this song.

lines.여호와께서 집을 세우지 않으시면: Unless the Lord builds the house
lines.여호와께서 성을 지키지 않으시면: Unless the Lord guards the city
lines.파수꾼이 깨어 있어도 헛되리: the watchman stays awake in vain
lines.일찍 일어나고 늦게 누워: Rising early and lying down late
lines.애써 얻은 떡을 먹어도 헛되네: eating hard-won bread is in vain
lines.여호와는 사랑하시는 이에게: For the Lord gives to those he loves
lines.보라 자식은 여호와께서 주신 기업: Children are a heritage from the Lord
lines.태의 열매는 그가 주신 상급: the fruit of the womb is his reward
lines.용사의 손에 든 화살 같으니: are like arrows in a warrior's hand
lines.화살통에 가득 채운 이는 복되리: Blessed is the one whose quiver is full
lines.성문에서 원수와 말할 때: When he speaks with enemies at the gate
lines.부끄러움을 당하지 않으리: he will not be put to shame
lines.모든 수고가 헛되니: all our labor is in vain

ps2.title: The King Set on Zion
ps2.intro: Just as Solomon was anointed at the Gihon spring, the kings of David's house took the throne in Zion. The apostles called this song the word spoken through the mouth of David. It is a song that says the king whom heaven has set in place will not be shaken, even when the nations rise up.

lines.민족들이 헛된 일을 꾸미는가: and the peoples plot in vain?
lines.세상 왕들이 일어서고: The kings of the earth rise up
lines.여호와와 그 기름 부음 받은 이를 치네: against the Lord and his anointed
lines.그들이 맨 줄을 끊고: Let us break their cords, they say
lines.하늘에 앉으신 이가 웃으시네: The One enthroned in heaven laughs
lines.내가 나의 왕을 세웠다: I have set my King in place
lines.내가 여호와의 명을 전하리라: I will proclaim the Lord's decree
lines.내게 구하라 나라들을 유업으로: Ask me, and I will give you the nations
lines.땅 끝까지 네 것으로 주리라: and the ends of the earth as your own
lines.세상의 재판관들아 교훈을 받으라: Be warned, judges of the earth
lines.그에게 피하는 이마다 복되리: Blessed are all who take refuge in him

ps84.title: How Lovely Is Your House
ps84.setting: A song of the sons of Korah — longing for the temple
ps84.intro: The sons of Korah were Levites who kept the temple gates and sang. Like pilgrims walking the long road up to Zion for the feasts, they sang this song longing for the house of the Lord.

lines.주의 장막이 얼마나 사랑스러운지: how lovely is your dwelling place
lines.내 영혼이 주의 뜰을 사모하여: My soul longs for your courts
lines.내 마음과 몸이 살아 계신 하나님께: My heart and flesh cry out for joy
lines.참새도 제 집을 얻고: Even the sparrow finds a home
lines.제비도 새끼 둘 둥지를 얻었네: the swallow a nest for her young
lines.주께 힘을 얻고: Blessed are those whose strength is in you
lines.마음에 시온 길이 있는 이는 복되네: whose hearts are set on the road to Zion
lines.바카 골짜기를 지날 때: As they pass through the Valley of Baca
lines.그곳을 샘이 솟는 곳이 되게 하고: they make it a place of springs
lines.힘을 얻고 또 얻어: They go from strength to strength
lines.시온에서 하나님 앞에 서리라: and appear before God in Zion
lines.주의 뜰에서 보내는 하루가: A single day in your courts
lines.다른 곳의 천 날보다 나으니: is better than a thousand elsewhere
lines.악인의 장막에 머무느니: Rather than dwell in the tents of the wicked
lines.내 하나님 집 문지기로 서리라: I'd keep the door of my God's house
lines.여호와 하나님은 해요 방패: The Lord God is a sun and shield
lines.주를 의지하는 이는 복되도다: Blessed is the one who trusts in you

ps87.title: Born in Zion
ps87.setting: The nations will say they were born in Zion
ps87.intro: This short song of the sons of Korah sings of Zion as the city where every people was born. Egypt and Babylon, Philistia, Tyre and Cush, even the names of nations that were once enemies are written among those born in Zion.

lines.그의 터는 거룩한 산 위에 있네: His foundation is on the holy mountain
lines.여호와께서 야곱의 모든 집보다: More than all the dwellings of Jacob
lines.시온의 문들을 사랑하시네: the Lord loves the gates of Zion
lines.너를 두고 영광스러운 일을 말하네: glorious things are spoken of you
lines.나를 아는 이 가운데 세리라: I will count among those who know me
lines.이 사람도 거기서 났다 하리라: This one was born there, they will say
lines.이 사람 저 사람이 거기서 났다: This one and that one were born there
lines.시온을 두고 말하리라: So it will be said of Zion
lines.여호와께서 민족들을 적으실 때: When the Lord registers the peoples
lines.이 사람이 거기서 났다 기록하시리: he will write, This one was born there
lines.나의 모든 샘이 네게 있다 하리라: will say, All my springs are in you
lines.나의 모든 샘이 네게 있네: All my springs are in you

ps48.title: The Song of Zion
ps48.intro: This is a song of Zion sung by the sons of Korah. It sings of kings who gathered to attack the city, saw it, and fled in terror. It calls the people to count the towers and walls of Zion, where the temple stands, and to tell it to the next generation.

lines.우리 하나님의 성 거룩한 산에서: in the city of our God, on his holy mountain
lines.온 세상의 기쁨이로다: the joy of the whole earth
lines.북쪽 끝에 선 큰 왕의 성: The city of the great King, in the far north
lines.자신을 피난처로 알리셨네: has shown himself to be her refuge
lines.왕들이 모여 함께 지나가다: The kings gathered and advanced together
lines.그 성을 보고 놀라: They saw the city and were astounded
lines.두려워 서둘러 달아났네: Terrified, they hurried away in flight
lines.해산하는 여인처럼 떨었네: They trembled like a woman in labor
lines.땅 끝까지 이르네: reaches to the ends of the earth
lines.시온을 두루 걸으며 망대들을 세어 보라: Walk about Zion and count her towers
lines.성벽을 살피고 궁궐을 둘러보라: Consider her walls, go through her citadels
lines.다음 세대에 전하여 주라: Tell it to the next generation
lines.이 하나님은 영원히 우리 하나님: This God is our God forever
lines.죽을 때까지 우리를 이끄시리: He will guide us until death

ps120.title: A Stranger in Meshech
ps120.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps120.intro: There was a stranger who lived among the tents of a foreign people, in Meshech and Kedar. Worn out by lying tongues and endless quarrels, he at last set out on the road up to Jerusalem. The Songs of Ascents begin with that departure.

lines.환난 중에 내가 여호와께 부르짖자: In my distress I cried to the Lord
lines.속이는 혀에서 나를 건지소서: from a deceitful tongue, deliver me
lines.내게 화로다 메섹에 머무는 나: Woe to me, who dwells in Meshech
lines.게달의 장막 사이에 사는 나: who lives among the tents of Kedar
lines.너무 오래 머물렀네: I have lived far too long
lines.속이는 혀여 네가 무엇을 받으랴: What will you get, deceitful tongue?
lines.로뎀나무 숯불이라: and burning coals of the broom tree
lines.내가 말하면 그들은 싸우려 하네: but when I speak, they are for war

ps121.title: To the Hills
ps121.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps121.intro: The pilgrims who set out walked for many days. At last the hills of Judah came into view in the distance. With slippery slopes, the blazing midday sun, and cold night roads ahead of them, they lifted their eyes and sang this song to one another.

lines.내가 눈을 들어 산을 보네: I lift my eyes and look to the hills
lines.나의 도움 어디서 올까: Where will my help come from?
lines.나의 도움은 여호와에게서: My help comes from the Lord
lines.하늘과 땅을 지으신 분: the Maker of heaven and earth
lines.주께서 네 발이 미끄러지지 않게 하시리: He will not let your foot slip
lines.너를 지키시는 이는 졸지 않으시네: The One who keeps you will not slumber
lines.여호와는 너를 지키는 이: The Lord is the one who keeps you
lines.네 오른편의 그늘이 되시니: He is the shade at your right hand
lines.낮의 해도 너를 상하지 않고: The sun will not harm you by day
lines.모든 환난을 면하게 하시고: He will keep you from all harm
lines.너의 나가고 들어옴을: Your going out and your coming in
lines.이제부터 영원까지 지키시리: he will keep, now and forevermore

ps122.title: Let Us Go to the House of the Lord
ps122.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps122.intro: At last the pilgrims' feet stood within the gates of Jerusalem. The voices that had called to one another on the day they set out, Let us go up to the house of the Lord, still rang in their ears. Inside the gates they sang this song, handed down as a psalm of David.

lines.여호와의 집에 올라가자 할 때: When they said, Let us go up to the Lord
lines.예루살렘아 잘 짜인 성읍: Jerusalem, a city closely built together
lines.여러 지파 여호와의 지파들이: The tribes, the tribes of the Lord
lines.이스라엘의 법도를 따라: as the law of Israel commands
lines.주의 이름에 감사하러 오르네: go up to give thanks to his name
lines.예루살렘의 평안을 위해 구하라: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem
lines.너를 사랑하는 이들이 형통하리: May those who love you prosper
lines.네 성 안에 평안이 있고: May there be peace within your walls
lines.내 형제와 친구를 위하여: For my brothers and friends' sake
lines.우리 하나님 여호와의 집을 위하여: For the house of the Lord our God

ps123.title: I Lift My Eyes
ps123.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps123.intro: Among the pilgrims who entered the city were some who had long been looked down on. The scorn of the comfortable and the contempt of the proud had piled up behind their backs. Like servants watching their master's hand, they lifted their eyes to heaven.

lines.내가 눈을 들어 주를 봅니다: I lift up my eyes to you
lines.종의 눈이 주인의 손을: As a servant's eyes watch his master's hand
lines.여종의 눈이 여주인의 손을 보듯: as a maid's eyes watch her mistress's hand
lines.우리 눈이 여호와를 바라보네: so our eyes look to the Lord
lines.우리를 불쌍히 여기실 때까지: until he has mercy on us
lines.여호와여 우리를 긍휼히 여기소서: Have mercy on us, O Lord
lines.멸시가 우리에게 넘쳤습니다: We have had more than enough contempt

ps124.title: If the Lord Had Not Been on Our Side
ps124.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps124.intro: The pilgrims sat together in a circle and talked of days gone by. There had been days when enemies swept over them like a flood and they were nearly swallowed up. When one person began this song, handed down as a psalm of David, everyone joined in.

lines.여호와께서 우리 편이 아니셨다면: If the Lord had not been on our side
lines.사람들이 우리를 치러 일어났을 때: when people rose up against us
lines.그들의 노여움이 불붙듯 할 때: when their anger flared like fire
lines.우리를 산 채로 삼켰으리: they would have swallowed us alive
lines.물이 우리를 덮치고: The waters would have engulfed us
lines.시내가 우리 영혼을 휩쓸었으리: the torrent would have swept over our souls
lines.우리를 그들 이에 내주지 않으셨네: who did not give us to their teeth
lines.새가 사냥꾼의 올무에서 벗어나듯: Like a bird escaping the fowler's snare
lines.올무가 끊어지고 우리가 벗어났네: the snare is broken and we are free
lines.우리의 도움은 여호와의 이름에 있네: Our help is in the name of the Lord
lines.하늘과 땅을 지으신 이의 이름에: in the name of the Maker of heaven and earth
lines.하늘과 땅을 지으신 이: the Maker of heaven and earth

ps125.title: Jerusalem Ringed by Mountains
ps125.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps125.intro: Looking up from inside the city, they could see the mountains surrounding Jerusalem. The Mount of Olives to the east and the hills to the south and west held the city in their embrace. Looking at those mountains, the pilgrims sang that the Lord surrounds his people.

lines.여호와를 의지하는 사람은: Those who trust in the Lord
lines.이제부터 영원까지: from this time on and forever
lines.의인의 땅에 머물지 못하리니: will not remain on the land of the righteous
lines.의인이 손을 뻗어: so that the righteous may not reach out
lines.여호와여 선한 이에게: O Lord, do good to those who are good
lines.마음이 바른 이에게 선을 베푸소서: to those who are upright in heart

ps126.title: Like Those Who Dream
ps126.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps126.intro: Among the pilgrims there were probably descendants of those who had returned from captivity in Babylon. They remembered the laughter of the day they came back to Zion as if it were a dream. Yet seeing the land still dry, they sang this song with the heart of one who sows seed in tears.

lines.우리는 꿈꾸는 것 같았네: we were like those who dream
lines.입에는 웃음이 가득하고: Our mouths were filled with laughter
lines.여호와께서 그들에게 큰일을 하셨다: The Lord has done great things for them
lines.여호와께서 우리에게 큰일을 하셨으니: The Lord has done great things for us
lines.울며 씨를 메고 나간 이는: Those who go out weeping, carrying seed
lines.기쁨으로 단을 안고 돌아오리라: will come home with joy, carrying sheaves

ps128.title: Children around Your Table
ps128.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps128.intro: As the sun went down, the pilgrims sat down by families and shared their food. Looking at the children seated around the table, the fathers sang of the blessing that comes upon a house that fears the Lord.

lines.여호와를 경외하며: Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord
lines.네 손이 수고한 대로 먹으리니: You will eat the fruit of your labor
lines.네가 복되고 형통하리라: You will be blessed and prosper
lines.열매 맺는 포도나무 같고: will be like a fruitful vine
lines.여호와께서 시온에서 네게 복 주시리니: May the Lord bless you from Zion
lines.평생에 예루살렘의 번영을 보고: May you see Jerusalem prosper all your life

ps129.title: Plowmen on My Back
ps129.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps129.intro: By the lamplight, the older pilgrims recalled what they had endured since their youth. From her youth Israel had been trampled countless times, yet she was never broken. Remembering wounds cut deep like furrows in a field, they sang this song.

lines.내가 어릴 때부터 그들이 나를 괴롭혔네: They have afflicted me since my youth
lines.나를 이기지 못하였네: yet they have not prevailed over me
lines.밭 가는 자들이 내 등을 갈아: The plowmen plowed upon my back
lines.의로우신 여호와께서: But the Lord, who is righteous
lines.악인의 줄을 끊으셨네: has cut the cords of the wicked
lines.부끄러워 물러가리라: will be put to shame and turned back
lines.지붕 위의 풀과 같아서: They will be like grass on the rooftops
lines.베는 자의 손에 차지 않고: It will not fill the reaper's hand
lines.묶는 자의 품에도 차지 않으리: nor the arms of the one who binds sheaves

ps130.title: Out of the Depths
ps130.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps130.intro: In the temple courts after sunset, each pilgrim called to mind his own sins. Like people drowning in deep water, they called on the Lord from the very bottom. And they waited for forgiveness as watchmen wait for the morning.

lines.여호와여 내가 깊은 곳에서: Out of the depths, O Lord
lines.나의 간구에 귀를 기울이소서: Let your ears attend to my plea
lines.주께서 죄악을 지켜보신다면: If you kept a record of sins
lines.그러나 사하심이 주께 있으니: But with you there is forgiveness
lines.주를 경외하게 하심이라: so that you may be feared
lines.내 영혼이 주를 기다리네: My soul waits for the Lord
lines.파수꾼이 아침을 기다림보다: More than watchmen wait for the morning
lines.내 영혼이 주를 더 기다리네: my soul waits for the Lord
lines.이스라엘아 여호와를 바라라: O Israel, hope in the Lord
lines.인자하심이 주께 있고: For with the Lord is steadfast love
lines.풍성한 속량이 주께 있으니: and with him is full redemption

ps131.title: Like a Weaned Child
ps131.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps131.intro: As the night grew deep, excited hearts grew quiet one by one. This short song, handed down as a psalm of David, sings of a heart that does not chase great things, but rests like a child in its mother's arms.

lines.여호와여 내 마음이 교만하지 않고: O Lord, my heart is not proud
lines.내 눈이 높지 않습니다: my eyes are not raised too high
lines.큰일과 내게 버거운 놀라운 일을: I do not chase great matters
lines.따라가려 하지 않습니다: or wonders too hard for me
lines.젖 뗀 아이가 어머니 품에 있듯: Like a weaned child with its mother
lines.내 영혼이 젖 뗀 아이 같습니다: my soul is like a weaned child
lines.이스라엘아 여호와를 바라라: O Israel, hope in the Lord
lines.이제부터 영원까지: from this time on and forever

ps133.title: When Brothers Live Together
ps133.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps133.intro: Pilgrims who had come up from many tribes gathered in one city. People from towns far and near sat down together, eating and singing. This song, handed down as a psalm of David, holds the joy of that gathering.

lines.머리 위에 부은 보배로운 기름이: It is like precious oil on the head
lines.수염 곧 아론의 수염을 타고: running down the beard, Aaron's beard
lines.그 옷깃까지 흘러내림 같고: flowing down to the collar of his robes
lines.헤르몬의 이슬이: It is like the dew of Hermon
lines.시온의 산들에 내림 같구나: falling on the mountains of Zion
lines.거기서 여호와께서 복을 명하셨으니: For there the Lord commanded the blessing

ps134.title: Toward the Sanctuary by Night
ps134.setting: A pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem
ps134.intro: On the last night of the pilgrimage, there were servants in the temple who stood and served in the house of the Lord even at night. When the pilgrims called to them to bless the Lord, an answer blessing them from Zion would likely have come back from within. The Songs of Ascents end here.

lines.보라 밤에 여호와의 집에 서 있는: Come, all you servants of the Lord

ps46.title: Refuge
ps46.intro: In the days of Hezekiah, the army of Sennacherib, king of Assyria, struck the towns of Judah and surrounded Jerusalem. The king went up to the temple and prayed, and that night the angel of the Lord struck the Assyrian camp. This song of the sons of Korah was likely sung inside the city around that time.

lines.하나님은 우리의 피난처 우리의 힘: God is our refuge and our strength

ps74.title: The Burned Sanctuary
ps74.intro: The Babylonian army entered Jerusalem and burned the temple of the Lord. This teaching psalm bearing Asaph's name was likely the lament of those who stood before the scorched sanctuary. It was a day when no signs were seen and no prophet remained.

ps79.title: The Nations Have Entered Your Inheritance
ps79.intro: It was the day Jerusalem became a heap of rubble, and there was no one to bury those who had fallen in the streets. This song bearing Asaph's name is the prayer of those left in the ruined city, crying out to God, How long?

lines.주의 거룩한 성전을 더럽히고: They have defiled your holy temple

ps89.title: Where Is the House of David?
ps89.intro: This is a teaching psalm of Ethan the Ezrahite. It sings of the covenant that promised David an everlasting throne, and then the song stops before a crown thrown to the ground. On the day the throne of David's house was overturned and its walls fell, which many place around the Babylonian exile, it asks where that covenant is now.

ps137.title: By the Rivers of Babylon
ps137.intro: Jerusalem fell, and the people were carried off to Babylon. In a strange land of great rivers and canals, their captors told them to sing one of the songs of Zion. They hung their harps on the willows and wept.

ps102.title: Prayer of the Afflicted
ps102.intro: The heading calls this song the prayer of one who is afflicted, who grows faint and pours out his complaint before the Lord. Since it cherishes even the stones and dust of Zion as it waits for the time when God will rebuild it, it was probably a lament sung in the days of exile.

ps85.title: Revive Us Again
ps85.setting: The land the exiles returned to
ps85.intro: By the decree of Cyrus, king of Persia, the exiles returned to Jerusalem. But the land they came back to lay in ruins, and their hearts were still heavy. This song of the sons of Korah asks the God who brought them back to revive them again.

ps118.title: Hosanna
ps118.intro: Before the Passover, Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a young donkey. The crowds spread their cloaks and branches on the road and shouted, Hosanna to the Son of David! ps41.title: The Friend Who Shared My Bread
ps41.intro: At the last Passover supper, after washing the disciples' feet, Jesus said that this was to fulfill the Scripture, The one who eats my bread has lifted his heel against me. Judas took the piece of bread and went out at once into the night.

ps22.title: My God, Why
ps22.intro: From noon on Friday, darkness covered the whole land. At about three in the afternoon, Jesus cried out with a loud voice from the cross, Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani. It was the first line of David's Psalm 22. This song begins with a cry of abandonment and ends with the praise of the whole earth.

ps31.title: Into Your Hands
ps31.intro: In the afternoon, when the sun had lost its light, Jesus called out with a loud voice from the cross, Father, into your hands I commit my spirit. He offered a line of Psalm 31, which David sang while being hunted, with his last breath, and breathed his last.

ps16.title: Not to See Decay
ps16.intro: At Pentecost, Peter stood up before the crowd gathered in Jerusalem. He quoted David's Psalm 16 and said that David died and his tomb is with us to this day, but this song was spoken looking ahead to Christ, who did not see decay but rose again.

ps110.title: Sit at My Right Hand
ps110.intro: The risen Jesus led his disciples out as far as Bethany, lifted up his hands and blessed them, and was taken up into heaven before their eyes. At Pentecost, Peter quoted David's Psalm 110 and proclaimed, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand.

lines.여호와께서 맹세하셨으니: The Lord has sworn an oath
lines.그 뜻을 돌이키지 않으시리라: and he will not change his mind
lines.주께서 주의 오른쪽에 계시니: The Lord is at your right hand
lines.길가의 시냇물을 마시고: He will drink from the brook by the way

ps146.title: I Will Praise Him All My Life
ps146.intro: The last five songs of the Psalms all open with Hallelujah and close with Hallelujah. The first of them was one person's confession: do not trust in mortals, who return to the dust when their breath departs, but put your hope in the Lord who made heaven and earth.

lines.내 영혼아 여호와를 찬양하라: Praise the Lord, O my soul
lines.나 사는 동안 여호와를 찬양하고: I will praise the Lord as long as I live
lines.내 숨이 있는 날 동안: As long as I have breath
lines.나의 하나님을 노래하리라: I will sing to my God
lines.힘 있는 사람들을 의지하지 말라: Do not put your trust in the powerful
lines.숨이 끊어지면 흙으로 돌아가니: Their breath departs, they return to dust
lines.그 날에 그 생각도 사라지리: and on that day their plans perish
lines.야곱의 하나님을 도움으로 삼고: Blessed is the one whose help is Jacob's God
lines.여호와께 소망을 두는 자는 복이 있네: whose hope is in the Lord
lines.하늘과 땅과 바다를 지으신 분: The Maker of heaven, earth, and sea
lines.억눌린 이에게 정의를 베푸시고: He gives justice to the oppressed
lines.눈먼 자의 눈을 여시네: and opens the eyes of the blind
lines.구부러진 자를 일으키시고: He lifts up those who are bowed down
lines.고아와 과부를 붙드시네: and upholds the orphan and the widow
lines.시온아 여호와는 영원히 다스리시리: O Zion, the Lord will reign forever
lines.너의 하나님이 대대로 다스리시리: Your God will reign for all generations
lines.야곱의 하나님을 도움으로 삼는 자는: Whoever makes Jacob's God their help

ps147.title: The Healer of Broken Hearts
ps147.intro: This song was likely sung when ruined Jerusalem was being rebuilt and the scattered people were coming home. It praised the One who counts the stars of heaven and calls each by name, who heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.

lines.우리 하나님을 찬송함이 선하니: How good it is to sing praise to our God
lines.별의 수를 세시고: He counts the number of the stars
lines.하나하나 이름을 부르시네: and calls each one by name
lines.구름으로 하늘을 덮으시고: He covers the sky with clouds
lines.땅을 위하여 비를 마련하시네: and prepares rain for the earth
lines.산에 풀이 자라게 하시고: He makes grass grow on the hills
lines.우는 까마귀 새끼도 먹이시네: and feeds even the young ravens that cry
lines.말의 힘을 기뻐하지 않으시고: He takes no delight in the horse's strength
lines.사람의 다리를 즐거워하지 않으시네: nor pleasure in the legs of a man
lines.주를 경외하는 자들을: He delights in those who fear him
lines.그 인자를 바라는 자들을 기뻐하시네: who hope in his steadfast love
lines.말씀을 보내 그것들을 녹이시니: He sends his word and melts them
lines.바람이 불고 물이 흐르네: the wind blows and the waters flow

ps148.title: Praise Him from the Heavens
ps148.intro: The third of the five Hallelujah songs calls on the whole world. It summons in turn the angels of heaven, sun, moon, and stars, the seas, mountains, trees, and beasts of the earth, kings and peoples, the old and the young, and tells them all to praise the name of the Lord together.

lines.하늘에서 여호와를 찬양하라: Praise the Lord from the heavens
lines.빛나는 별들아 찬양하라: Praise him, all you shining stars
lines.그가 명하시매 지음을 받았도다: He commanded and they were created
lines.여호와의 이름을 찬양하라: Praise the name of the Lord
lines.그 이름만 홀로 높으시니: for his name alone is exalted
lines.그 영광이 땅과 하늘 위에: His glory over earth and sky
lines.땅에서 여호와를 찬양하라: Praise the Lord from the earth
lines.바다의 큰 물고기와 깊은 바다들아: Great sea creatures and all ocean depths
lines.불과 우박과 눈과 안개: Fire and hail, snow and mist
lines.말씀을 따르는 거센 바람아: stormy winds that obey his word
lines.들짐승과 가축과 나는 새들: wild animals, cattle, and flying birds
lines.세상의 왕들과 모든 백성들: kings of the earth and all peoples
lines.청년과 처녀 노인과 아이들아: young men and maidens, old and young

ps149.title: With a New Song
ps149.intro: The fourth of the five Hallelujah songs was a new song sung in the assembly of the saints. With tambourines and harps the people danced and rejoiced in their Maker and their King. It was a song that the Lord delights in his people and crowns the humble with salvation.

lines.새 노래로 여호와께 노래하라: Sing to the Lord a new song
lines.성도의 모임 가운데서 찬양하라: Praise him in the assembly of the saints
lines.이스라엘아 지으신 이를 기뻐하라: Let Israel rejoice in their Maker
lines.시온의 자녀들아 너의 왕을 즐거워하라: Children of Zion, be glad in your King
lines.여호와께서 자기 백성을 기뻐하시고: For the Lord delights in his people
lines.낮은 자를 구원으로 아름답게 하시네: He crowns the humble with salvation
lines.성도들아 영광 중에 즐거워하라: Let the saints rejoice in glory
lines.누운 자리에서도 기뻐 노래하라: Let them sing for joy on their beds
lines.입에는 하나님을 높이는 찬양: Praise of God in their mouths
lines.주의 공의가 이 땅에 서리라: His justice will stand on this earth
lines.이것이 모든 성도의 영광: This is the glory of all his saints

ps150.title: Hallelujah
ps150.setting: Hallelujah 5: the last song of the Psalms
ps150.intro: In the last song of the Psalms there is no lament and no enemy. It calls for praise in the sanctuary and in the mighty heavens, with trumpet, harp, lyre, tambourine, flute, and cymbals, and it calls on everything that breathes. The song that came through nights of flight and fallen cities has at last arrived at Hallelujah.

lines.권능의 하늘에서 찬양하라: Praise him in his mighty heavens
lines.그의 크신 일을 인하여 찬양하라: Praise him for his mighty deeds
lines.그 위대하심을 따라 찬양하라: Praise him for his surpassing greatness
lines.나팔 소리로 찬양하라: Praise him with the trumpet's sound
lines.비파와 수금으로 찬양하라: Praise him with harp and lyre
lines.소고 치며 춤추어 찬양하라: Praise him with tambourine and dancing
lines.현악과 피리로 찬양하라: Praise him with strings and flute
